changes.idle_packet_gate: One atomic load replaces the empty-map shard scan.
changes.source_packet_stack: Allocate on demand and reuse until address change or shutdown.
changes.route_updates: Publish configuration and service routes before packet dispatch.
changes.admission_repair: Wait for bounded queue capacity after reserving the existing stream and memory permits.

verification.source_review: No remaining actionable findings after both repairs.

predictions.before: With a proxy listener enabled and no registered packet consumers, the batch filter traverses N packets and parses eligible headers.
predictions.after: One atomic entry-count load returns each idle batch before parsing packets.
predictions.dominant_saved_cost: N header inspections with an enabled listener, or S shard locks per idle batch in the old empty-map gate
predictions.shards: DashMap uses next_power_of_two(4 times available_parallelism) shards. The 16-core local host uses 64.
predictions.memory: Avoids temporary packet-batch vectors on the inactive path.

predictions.before: Listener startup can retain a reactor, two forwarding tasks, one task collector, two device channels, and three packet queues.
predictions.after: The stack state appears only when a packet consumer needs it.
predictions.memory: Avoids fixed stack and queue storage in stream-only use. TCP payload buffers are allocated per socket and are not an idle-stack saving.
predictions.constraint: The GUI and FFI listeners are real packet consumers. Their stack remains allocated.

predictions.before: IP batch routing and ordered sending refresh path configuration. Changed topology routes are copied into a second store during sending.
predictions.after: Configuration setters update path state. Route publication publishes combined service routes.
predictions.dominant_saved_cost: Repeated per-batch update checks and local-address atomic swaps
predictions.memory: Topology-only instances share O(R) immutable prefix tables. Instances with local routes build O(R+L) combined route data on updates.
predictions.constraint: Authorization and route-generation validation remain at dispatch boundaries.

predictions.before: Each enabled experimental stream owns three bounded channels, one command channel, a session task, two ordered reliability windows, and retry timers.
predictions.after: Eligible TCP traffic uses an existing authenticated HTTP/3 stream. Other TCP traffic uses the retained packet stack.
predictions.memory: Compiled code decreases. Active packet-stack memory can exceed the removed custom stream windows.
predictions.constraint: Do not claim an idle endpoint saving when the experiment was already disabled.

measurement_contract.payload_integrity: Compare every delivered byte with a repeated known block.
measurement_contract.cpu: Sum of both LowTier endpoint processes and the relay when present, normalized by delivered Gbit.
measurement_contract.rss: Process RSS sampled every 100 milliseconds; retain idle, minimum, and maximum.
measurement_contract.latency: Twenty-one application echo samples per process set.
measurement_contract.loss: Record delivery ratio and QUIC path lost-packet counters.
measurement_contract.limitations: Loopback results do not establish WAN performance. Native fleet routes use the automatic protocol policy.
measurement_contract.tcp_loss: H2/WSS captures cover the isolated listener port. Capture drops must be zero. Native TCP_INFO covers the exact application connection.
measurement_contract.connection_setup: Accepted throughput measurements establish connections before timing. The burst regression test separately verifies concurrent admission.

fixture_correction.before: The local validator allocated and copied 128 KiB for each recv call, in addition to the expected byte slice.
fixture_correction.after: The validator reuses one 128 KiB pattern. The exact comparison still covers every received byte.
fixture_correction.saved_traffic: 128 KiB multiplied by recv call count
fixture_correction.evidence: Preserve every earlier result. Final candidate comparisons use release- groups. Accepted overlay groups retain the unchanged experimental reference.

native_comparison.transport: Automatic fleet policy; the underlying protocol was not isolated.

limitations: Whole-tunnel throughput and sampled RSS results are mixed. No universal speed or memory gain is established.
Local measurements use loopback. They do not establish WAN throughput.
CPU covers LowTier processes. Other processes and kernel work charged elsewhere are excluded.
RSS is sampled every 100 milliseconds and is summed across participating LowTier processes.
The local matrix uses three transfers per direction. Additional baseline process starts showed variation.
Native runs use automatic transport selection. They cannot isolate a transport or establish a universal version ranking.
The intermediate candidate had a higher native upload rate in a separate automatic-route run. That run does not establish a matched transport ranking.
The GUI and FFI can require the source packet stack. Lazy allocation does not remove that required state.
The unchanged parallel-suite logging assertion remains outside accepted sequential verification.
Stripped release profiles do not identify individual Rust functions.
recovered_failures: HTTP/3 request bursts received false 503 replies before bounded queue admission was repaired.
The idle gate waited for a DashMap shard before the atomic-only gate was installed.
The first TCP capture retained packets in the kernel. Immediate capture mode recovered the evidence.
The timed native fixture ended with queued bytes. The replacement verifies exact receiver bytes.
An initial local benchmark validator allocated 128 KiB per read. Final measurements reuse a fixed pattern.
Local protected configuration records were recovered from verified pre-install references.
The old local node lost routes to restarted peers. Its planned update restored routes and delivery.
The router upload timed out. A verified 8879849-byte prefix allowed the remaining transfer to resume.
The router restart returned before the new process was ready. Its new PID and running image were verified afterward.
The viewer required a restart to include the new source page in its file allowlist.
The cleanup audit first included an offline historical host. It was corrected to inspect the eleven deployed hosts.
